title: PEARL: FPGA-Based Reinforcement Learning Acceleration with Pipelined Parallel Environments
problem: CPU-based RL frameworks struggle with slow multi-environment update computation; parallelizing environments requires efficient data transfer and computation overlap.
motivation: RL training heavily depends on parallelizing environment interactions to collect training data efficiently; software frameworks face I/O and compute bottlenecks.
method: FPGA-based framework that instantiates multiple parallel environments with pipelined execution scheme. Pipeline design hides data transfer latency within computation time. Flexible environment definition allows users to add custom environments. Supports scaling from 1024 to 43008+ environments.
key_novelty: Pipelined parallel environment architecture that overlaps data transfer with computation, eliminating I/O bottleneck for multi-environment RL training.
contributions: 4.36-972.6x speedup over fastest software framework for parallel environment execution
Scales to 43008 environments with marginal power increase (3%)
Flexible environment framework for custom RL tasks
7-15% training time reduction when integrated with existing RL algorithms

metrics.other: 3% power increase at 43008 envs, 2.24x LUT, 3.08x FF utilization

limitations: FPGA-specific; applicability to cloud-scale distributed RL systems not discussed; memory bandwidth constraints for very large environments not addressed.
primary_theme: FPGA-accelerated parallel RL environments via pipelined dataflow
